name: Citizenship by descent and by registration of birth

requirement_groups.name: Born in Singapore to at least one citizen or PR parent

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being born in Singapore with at least one parent who was a Singapore citizen or permanent resident at the time of birth — Singapore does not have unconditional jus soli; birth in Singapore alone, to two non-resident foreign parents, does not confer citizenship.

requirement_groups.name: Born abroad to a Singapore citizen parent

requirements.blocker_text: This requires at least one parent being a Singapore citizen at the time of your birth abroad. Registration with ICA is required — citizenship by descent is not automatically recorded without it.

evidence_required.document: Birth certificate and evidence of the qualifying parent's citizenship or PR status at the time of birth

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL CONTRAST with several other countries in this dataset: Singapore does NOT have unconditional jus soli — being born on Singapore soil to two non-citizen, non-PR foreign parents does not itself confer citizenship, a materially more restrictive position than France's or Japan's automatic parent-based attribution, and closer in spirit to Ireland's post-2005 reformed birthright rules (fr_droit_du_sang_et_du_sol notes the contrast; ie_ prior research flagged Ireland's similar 2005 tightening) than to the more permissive historical Anglo-American jus soli tradition. Dual citizenship is not permitted upon reaching adulthood — children who acquire another nationality alongside Singapore citizenship at birth must formally renounce the other by age 21, the same structural pattern as Japan's age-25 choice-of-nationality requirement (jp_citizenship_descent) but with a different, earlier age cutoff — a genuine cross-country comparison point worth surfacing. No confirmed generational limit beyond the direct parent-child link — like France and Japan, Singapore's descent rule applies based on a PARENT's citizenship specifically, not extended to grandparents the way Portugal's or UK Ancestry's routes reach further back.
